newsitem.title: HONG KONG: CKI seen easily making 96 results target.
newsitem.headline: CKI seen easily making 96 results target.

text.p: Cheung Kong Infrastructure Holdings Ltd (CKI) is expected to have little difficulty making its 1996 earnings forecast, analysts said on Tuesday.
The results for the year ended December 31 will be released on Thursday in the first annual report to be issued since the company was listed in June 1996.
At the time of listing, CKI forecast earnings of not less than HK$728 million (US$94 million), but analysts were more bullish.
Better-than-expected results from the cement and concrete divisions boosted HSBC James Capel's expectations to HK$800 million.
"We have seen a stronger market and better prices in these key markets," said HSBC analyst Leon Chik.
Asia Equity analyst Bee Lim said in a recent report that he was expecting earnings of HK$771 million.
"Of the total...73 percent will come from the building materials division, 14 percent from power plant projects and 12 percent from toll road and bridges," Lim said.
CKI is an amalgamation of companies and projects in the Cheung Kong (Holdings) Ltd group spun off last year.

Its main components include Green Island Cement (Holding) Ltd, an integrated cement manufacturer and distributor, and Anderson Asia (Holdings) Ltd, which produces and distributes concrete and quarries and sells aggregates.
Green Island is the largest cement manufacturer in Hong Kong with an estimated market share of 47 percent.
CKI is also the vehicle for the Cheung Kong group's infrastructure investments in China, including power plants, toll roads, and toll bridges in China.

At the time of listing, the company had invested in 19 infrastructural development projects in China, chiefly in Guangdong province. Of those, 13 were toll road and bridge projects and the remaining six were power plants.
The company has since added several more China infrastructure projects to its portfolio.
Two new projects -- the Jiangmen highway and Shenyang toll road and bridge -- acquired after the listing will make a small additional contribution to second half profits, said Chik.

The company reported profit attributable to shareholders of HK$347.2 million for the six months ended June 30, 1996, a 43.89 percent increase over the pro forma profit and loss statement for first-half 1995.

The Cheung Kong group's restructuring announced in January 1997, which put Hongkong Electric Holdings Ltd (HKE) under CKI, will not have any impact on 1996 earnings. But it has had an impact on the share price.

"Before the HKE acquisition, we were becoming increasingly uncomfortable with CKI's stretched valuation. Issuing shares to pay for its interest in HKE was both PER (price earnings ratio) and NAV (net asset value) enhancing," said Asia Equity's Lim.
Lim calculates CKI's net asset value at HK$17.26 as of end-February 1997.
CKI shares, which were offered at HK$12.65 last year, closed HK$0.35 higher at HK$20.45 on Monday.
